stories.title: Mamdani Scores Critical Court Victory for Rent Freeze
stories.excerpt: Just ahead of the Thanksgiving weekend, a Manhattan Supreme Court judge sided with New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani on his controversial rent freeze in a case that landlords brought against the New York City Rent Guidelines Board (RGB). The mayor called the decision “a victory for tenants, for affordability and for the principle that working New Yorkers deserve a city they can afford to live in.” The case stems from a 7-1 vote by the mayor-appointed RGB on June 26 halting rent increases for the city’s approximately 1 million rent-stabilized apartments. The judge in today’s ruling, Brendan T. Lantry, emphasized that his decision was not a vote for or against the wisdom of the RGB’s ruling, and that it “may cause negative collateral consequences,” but that the rent freeze was nevertheless legal. In a lawsuit filed in July, landlords had contended that the RGB ignored evidence of the rising expenses that rent-stabilized owners face in maintaining and upgrading their buildings. In some cases, the landlords said, the RGB ignored its own data, which “clearly signaled a rent increase,” according to Ann Korchak, board president of Small Property Owners of New York, whose members were plaintiffs in the lawsuit. “This ruling is terribly disappointing to small property owners,” Korchak said in a statement on Wednesday. “The rent freeze will push more small rent-stabilized property owners to the edge of the cliff. It denies the resources they need to maintain and operate their rent-stabilized buildings. Property taxes, water and sewer rates, and insurance, energy, heating, repair and other costs and expenses aren’t frozen. bullets: NYC rent freeze for 1M rent-stabilized units upheld by Manhattan Supreme Court judge.
RGB voted 7-1 June 26 to halt increases; landlords argued rising maintenance costs ignored.
Judge acknowledged ruling may cause negative collateral consequences but found it legally sound.
stories.summary: A Manhattan Supreme Court judge upheld the New York City Rent Guidelines Board's controversial 7-1 vote in June to freeze rents on approximately 1 million rent-stabilized apartments. Landlords who sued argued the RGB ignored evidence of rising building maintenance and upgrade expenses. Judge Brendan Lantry ruled the freeze was legal despite potential negative consequences, rejecting landlord claims the board acted arbitrarily.
stories.impact: NYC rent-stabilized freeze reduces owner cash flow and ROI on stabilized stock, dampening acquisition appeal and limiting capital recycling for new multifamily development. However, it narrows arbitrage opportunities between stabilized and market-rate rents, making new market-rate development—especially luxury—more attractive to investors seeking unregulated economics. Flight from stabilized portfolios may accelerate, freeing some capital for new supply in outer boroughs and secondary markets.

stories.title: Netflix Acquiring Historic Radford Studio Center for $380M
stories.excerpt: Netflix has reached an agreement to acquire the historic Radford Studio Center in Studio City for a reported $380 million, marking the streaming giant’s first purchase of a Los Angeles-area studio lot. The property is located at 4024 Radford Avenue, just off Ventura Blvd in the southeastern San Fernando Valley, close to Hollywood, Burbank and many other entertainment-related businesses. As reported by the L.A. Times and other sources, Goldman Sachs took control of the property in January after its previous owner, Hackman Capital Partners, defaulted on a $1.1 billion mortgage amid a slowdown in Hollywood production. Hackman and Square Mile Capital Management acquired the property for $1.85 billion in 2021. The 1.14 million-square-foot production campus features 22 soundstages, 18 office buildings and 20 bungalows. Founded in 1928 by filmmaker Mack Sennett, the studio has been home to numerous iconic television series, including Seinfeld, Gilligan’s Island, Will & Grace and The Mary Tyler Moore Show. The acquisition represents a significant expansion of Netflix’s Southern California real estate holdings. The company currently leases approximately 2 million square feet of office and soundstage space in Los Angeles. Netflix intends to retain Radford’s existing studio team and maintain operations at the production campus. bullets: Netflix acquires Radford Studio Center, Studio City for $380M; first LA studio lot purchase.
Goldman Sachs foreclosed after Hackman defaulted on $1.1B mortgage in 2021 acquisition.
1.14M SF campus with 22 soundstages; Netflix currently leases ~2M SF in LA.
stories.summary: Netflix reached an agreement to acquire the historic Radford Studio Center in Studio City for $380 million, marking its first purchase of an LA studio lot. The 1.14 million-square-foot property features 22 soundstages, 18 office buildings, and 20 bungalows. Goldman Sachs took control after Hackman Capital Partners defaulted on a $1.1 billion mortgage amid production slowdown; Netflix is consolidating its ~2 million square feet of LA real estate holdings.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to multifamily development. Netflix's studio acquisition signals stabilization in LA entertainment production post-slowdown, which could modestly support job and population retention in the LA market, but entertainment employment is too small a share of regional demand drivers to materially move multifamily fundamentals.

stories.title: Fairstead Closes $17M Affordable Housing Transaction in Oklahoma
stories.excerpt: Fairstead announced its $16.5 million acquisition of London Square Village Apartments, a 200-unit project-based Section 8 community in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, and plans for a comprehensive rehabilitation of the property. The transaction marks Fairstead’s first acquisition in Oklahoma. London Square Village Apartments consists of 200 units across 18 two-story residential buildings and a community center. The community includes 24 one-bedroom, 96 two-bedroom and 80 three-bedroom homes, with all units reserved for households earning at or below 60% of the area median income.  “Expanding into Oklahoma represents an important step in Fairstead’s mission to preserve sustainable, reliable affordable housing for communities across the country,” said Jeff Goldberg, Founder and CEO of Fairstead. The acquisition will preserve London Square Village Apartments as affordable housing through 4% federal LIHTC equity from R4 Capital and tax-exempt bond financing issued by the Oklahoma Housing Finance Agency, with R4 Capital also serving as lender. Join us for the Connect Midwest Multifamily conference on the afternoon of Tuesday, June 8, 2027, at Joe’s Live in Rosemont, Illinois. bullets: Fairstead acquires London Square Village, Oklahoma City: 200-unit Section 8 community for $16.5M.

stories.summary: Fairstead closed a $16.5 million acquisition of London Square Village Apartments, a 200-unit project-based Section 8 community in Oklahoma City, marking its first Oklahoma deal. All units serve households earning at or below 60% of area median income across three- and four-building configurations. R4 Capital provided 4% LIHTC equity and lender role; Oklahoma Housing Finance Agency issued tax-exempt bond financing.
stories.impact: Acquisition signals investor confidence in secondary-market affordable housing, particularly stabilized Section 8 properties with long-term income certainty. Oklahoma City's affordable housing pipeline strengthens, but as acquisition-of-existing rather than new development, it does not directly expand supply. However, Fairstead's market entry and capital deployment may encourage other institutional buyers to underwrite OK secondary markets, supporting future new construction finance availability.

stories.title: Dwight Capital Finances $52M Loan for Mixed-Use Multifamily Community in Michigan
stories.excerpt: Dwight Capital has closed a $52 million HUD 223(f) loan for Griffin Royal Oak, a 245-unit luxury mixed-use multifamily community in the heart of Royal Oak, Michigan. Developed by Singh Development, the property features a five-story residential building, an attached parking garage, and four ground-floor commercial spaces totaling 9,000 square feet. Strategically located near downtown Royal Oak, Griffin Royal Oak is surrounded by pedestrian-friendly sidewalks, boutiques, salons, and retail shops, and more than 70 restaurants. The property’s luxury residences, ground-floor retail, and walkable location reflect Singh Development’s focus on thoughtfully designed communities in desirable locations. “Griffin Royal Oak represents the type of community we have focused on developing for more than five decades—high-quality residential environments in strong, established markets,” said Saab Grewal of Singh Development. Dwight Capital’s Karnveer Bal and Alex Shoenfeld originated the loan on behalf of Singh Development, an established, family-owned real estate development and investment company. Join us for the Connect Midwest Multifamily conference on the afternoon of Tuesday, June 8, 2027, at Joe’s Live in Rosemont, Illinois. bullets: Dwight Capital closes $52M HUD 223(f) refinance for Griffin Royal Oak, Michigan; 245 units.

stories.summary: Dwight Capital closed a $52 million HUD 223(f) loan for Griffin Royal Oak, a 245-unit luxury mixed-use multifamily community in Royal Oak, Michigan. The property features a five-story residential tower, attached parking garage, and 9,000 square feet of ground-floor retail, strategically positioned near downtown walkability and dining. Singh Development developed the asset in a strong, established market.
stories.impact: HUD 223(f) permanent financing availability signals lender appetite for stabilized multifamily assets in strong Midwest submarkets; Royal Oak's walkable downtown positioning and retail integration reflect developer strategy to build resilient, Class A-equivalent communities outside major coastal metros. Successful financing here validates acquisition thesis for Midwest secondary markets and may encourage further institutional capital flows into Great Lakes multifamily development.

stories.title: Host Hotels Rounds Out $202M Brooklyn Hotel Buy With $29M Retail, Parking Acquisition
stories.excerpt: Host Hotels & Resorts has secured three retail spaces and an indoor parking area at its newly acquired hotel asset in Brooklyn’s Dumbo neighborhood. The Bethesda, Md.-based real estate investment trust, through the entity Brooklyn Bridge Hotel Owner, acquired the commercial condo units and parking space at 90 Furman Street from a Starwood Capital Group entity, according to property records filed Wednesday. All four properties were built in 2015, according to city tax records, and adjoin Host Hotel’s newest portfolio addition, 1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge at 60 Furman Street. Host Hotel acquired the hotel’s 85-year leasehold interest from Starwood in a $202 million all-cash deal announced earlier this month. The 195-key hotel marks a significant feather in Host Hotel’s cap, as the operator expects 1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge to be among its top 10 assets based on full-year estimates. A second agreement, this one concerning the takeover and restructuring of an existing $113 million debt on the properties at 90 Furman and 60 Furman Street, was also filed in city records Wednesday. The properties’ existing mortgage was previously held by Sumitomo Mitsui Banking, according to the filing, and has now been assigned to the entity TRS NY Lender. The same entity has previously been linked by The Real Deal to the New York State Teachers’ Retirement System of NYC, which financed Host Hotels’ 2024 purchase of Starwood’s 1 Hotel Central Park at 1414 Avenue of the Americas. That $265 million deal was in one of that year’s top 10 investment sales. Host Hotels’ recent acquisition of the Dumbo hotel came on the heels of a $127 million all-cash purchase of the 308-room Renaissance Dallas at Plano Legacy West Hotel in Texas. The seller was a joint venture of Paceline Equity Partners and Aravest. Spokespeople for Host Hotels and Starwood did not respond to requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Host Hotels acquires 90 Furman retail/parking condos in Brooklyn for $29M adjacent to 1 Hotel.
1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge (60 Furman): 195-key, 85-year leasehold, $202M all-cash Starwood deal.
Host expects hotel to rank top-10 asset; also restructured $113M existing debt on properties.
stories.summary: Host Hotels & Resorts acquired three retail spaces and an indoor parking area at 90 Furman Street in Brooklyn's Dumbo for $29 million, adjacent to its newly acquired 1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge at 60 Furman Street. The hotel deal—85-year leasehold for $202 million all-cash from Starwood—represents a significant addition to Host's portfolio, with management expecting it to rank among the company's top 10 assets. A parallel $113 million debt restructuring was also filed.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to multifamily development. This is a hotel/hospitality transaction in Dumbo, Brooklyn. However, Host's confidence in Dumbo real estate (a $200M+ investment signal) and its bundling of retail/parking with lodging underscores mixed-use viability in this submarket, which could signal to multifamily developers that Dumbo has sufficient density and transit to support residential intensification and that ground-floor retail/activation drives value.

stories.title: Thor Equities Buys San Francisco Office/Retail Asset for $50.5M, Lands $51.8M Loan
stories.excerpt: Thor Equities has acquired 55 Stockton Street, a boutique Class A office and retail property in San Francisco’s Union Square district, from Zaber Corporation for $50.5 million. The company also secured $51.8 million in acquisition financing from Prime Finance. Also known as the National Center Building, the eight-story, 136,714-square-foot property is situated at the corner of Stockton and O’Farrell streets, one block south of Union Square. Built in 1988 and renovated in 2023, the building features three floors of retail space with boutique office space above. Office tenants include Chalk AI, Harness and Taylor & Associates Architects. The acquisition expands Thor’s presence in the Union Square district. The firm acquired nearby 146 Geary St., home to Bang & Olufsen’s flagship store, for $20.5 million in August. Thor also owns 152 Geary St., occupied by Banana Republic. The property offers convenient access to public transportation and is surrounded by prominent retail, dining and hospitality destinations. Newmark’s Chris Kramer, Ricky Braha, Tim Polglase and Dante DiStefano arranged the financing on behalf of Thor Equities. stories.summary: Thor Equities acquired 55 Stockton Street, a Class A office and retail property in San Francisco's Union Square district, for $50.5 million. The 136,714-square-foot, eight-story building (built 1988, renovated 2023) features three floors of boutique retail and upper-floor office space. Thor secured $51.8 million in acquisition financing from Prime Finance and continues expanding its Union Square presence.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to multifamily development. This is an office/retail conversion play in San Francisco's core CBD. However, the transaction signals that institutional capital is willing to finance Class A office assets with retail components in prime CBD locations, suggesting that multifamily developers exploring SF office-to-residential conversions may face stiff competition for best-in-class buildings and should focus on secondary CBD or neighborhood retail-mixed-use opportunities outside Union Square.

stories.title: OC Investor Group Buys Two Apartment Properties in Venice
stories.excerpt: A group of private Orange County-based investors acquired two multifamily properties totaling 40 units in the coastal Los Angeles community of Venice for $14.23 million. The properties, located at 1400 and 1500 Venice Blvd., were sold by Advanced Real Estate Group. The transaction, which partly included 1031 exchange capital, worked out to $355,662 per unit and $430 per square foot. Colliers’ Kitty Wallace represented the seller and, along with colleague Andy Eberhard, also represented the buyers. Built in 1988 and 1985, respectively, the properties encompass 33,072 square feet of building area and offer 77 parking spaces. Neither property is subject to the City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance. The 31-unit property at 1400 Venice Blvd. features renovated interiors, a fitness center, a rooftop lounge and subterranean parking. The nine-unit property at 1500 Venice Blvd. sold above its asking price for approximately $3.43 million, representing a 5.13% capitalization rate. The new ownership plans to continue the previous ownership’s unit renovation program. Photo is of 1500 Venice Blvd. The post OC Investor Group Buys Two Apartment Properties in Venice appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Orange County investor group buys two Venice apartments: 40 units for $14.23M total.

stories.summary: An Orange County-based investor group acquired two multifamily properties totaling 40 units in Venice for $14.23 million, working out to $355,662 per unit and $430 per square foot. The 31-unit property at 1400 Venice Blvd. and 9-unit property at 1500 Venice Blvd. were built in 1988 and 1985 respectively and are not subject to LA's Rent Stabilization Ordinance. New ownership plans to continue renovation programs.
stories.impact: Venice acquisition at $355K/unit on older, non-RSO-protected stock signals continued investor appetite for coastal LA multifamily despite affordability pressure and regulatory risk. The 1031 exchange funding mix and renovation upside strategy reflect buy-and-hold value-add thesis. However, deal price and cap rate (5.13% on the 9-unit building) suggest limited margin for error; developers should monitor whether cap rates in Venice stabilize or compress further, signaling overheating, and consider suburban Westside alternatives with higher density upside.

stories.title: Flight to Quality Deepens Divide Among Major U.S. Office Markets
stories.excerpt: The U.S. office market is showing more signs of improvement, but the recovery remains uneven across the nation’s biggest cities. The national office vacancy rate declined 140 basis points annually to 17.2 percent in October, while average asking rents increased 1.5 percent to $33.30 per square foot, according to a report using Yardi data. Office sales totaled nearly $56.9 billion across 2,576 transactions through the first 10 months of 2026, with properties trading at an average of $197 per square foot. But the flight to quality is widening the performance gap between newer and older properties, the report found. Asking rents for Class A office space increased 2.5 percent over the past year, while rents for Class B space declined 0.3 percent. “Office employment growth doesn’t always translate into an office market rebound, and we are seeing significant market discrepancies,” Peter Kolaczynski, director of Yardi Research, said in the report. “One consistency, though, is that outdated and less amenitized buildings are facing the most pressure, while new deliveries are offering best-in-class product and obtaining rent premiums.” Manhattan led the nation’s largest office markets in investment volume, construction activity, asking rents and occupancy in October. Investors traded more than $6.2 billion worth of Manhattan office properties in the first 10 months of the year at an average of $533 per square foot. Meanwhile, Manhattan’s average asking rents increased 9.5 percent annually to $74.44 per square foot, more than double the national average. The borough also had 3.73 million square feet of office space under construction, the largest development pipeline in the country. Miami recorded the strongest annual office rent growth among the markets tracked, with asking rates jumping 12.8 percent to $63.58 per square foot. stories.summary: The U.S. office market is showing uneven signs of recovery. National office vacancy declined 140 basis points annually to 17.2 percent in October 2026, with average asking rents rising 1.5 percent to $33.30 per square foot. However, a widening flight-to-quality trend showed Class A rents increasing 2.5 percent while Class B rents declined 0.3 percent, with outdated and less amenitized buildings facing the most pressure. Office sales totaled $56.9 billion through October 2026.
stories.impact: Office market bifurcation creates tailwind for adaptive reuse and office-to-multifamily conversion in secondary and tertiary CBDs where Class B/C office stock is abundant and distressed. Developers should prioritize Class A office conversions in strong markets (Boston, DC, Denver submarkets with young talent and tech jobs), but recognize that weak older office assets in secondary markets may never reach conversion economics unless local multifamily demand surges. Capital scarcity in distressed office may lower acquisition prices, but construction-to-residential conversion costs remain high; underwrite carefully in market-dependent scenarios.

stories.title: RXR Supplies $140M Construction Loan for Miami Rental Development
stories.excerpt: RXR has funneled $140 million into the construction of a Live Local Act rental tower near the Aventura Mall in Miami-Dade County. Group P6 is developing the 363-unit Spoke Aventura at 2600 Northeast 203rd Street. The 21-story development will rise a block west from Biscayne Boulevard, about a mile north of the 2.8 million-square-foot indoor mall and the city’s Brightline station. Construction is expected to be completed in 2028, with Moss serving as a general contractor. Morris Betesh and Ronnie Levine of Arrow Real Estate Advisors brokered the loan. More than 40 percent of units will be priced at 120 percent of the area’s median income, in accordance with Florida’s Live Local Act, which provides tax breaks and speedy approvals for developers. Amenities will include a pool deck, a fitness center, a resident lounge, coworking space and a padel court, along with ground-floor retail and a 435-space parking garage. The Boca Raton-based development firm, led by Ignacio Diaz and Jose J. Padua, paid $16 million for the 1.3-acre site in 2024. “Spoke Aventura and Group P6 represent the high-quality, well-located multifamily projects and the high-quality sponsorship that RXR’s Capital Solutions strategy is pursuing,” Russ Young, RXR’s head of investments, said in a statement. RXR, led by Scott Rechler, is a major New York investor and developer, best known for owning trophy office buildings and large-scale redevelopment, including 1211 Avenue of the Americas and the Helmsley Building. Its lending in South Florida has remained limited to a few projects, including providing a mezzanine loan to another Live Local Act project last year. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: RXR provides $140M construction loan for Spoke Aventura, Miami-Dade; 363-unit rental tower.
21-story, Group P6 developer; 40%+ units at 120% AMI under Florida Live Local Act.
Completion 2028; near Aventura Mall, Brightline station; amenities: pool, fitness, coworking, padel, retail.
stories.summary: RXR provided $140 million in construction financing for Spoke Aventura, a 363-unit rental tower near Aventura Mall in Miami-Dade County, developed by Group P6. The 21-story building, expected to complete in 2028, will have more than 40 percent of units priced at 120 percent of area median income under Florida's Live Local Act, which offers tax breaks and expedited approvals. Amenities include pool, fitness center, coworking, padel court, ground-floor retail, and 435-space parking garage.
stories.impact: Live Local Act financing cascade into Miami-Dade is accelerating supply in suburban nodes (Aventura) with transit connectivity (Brightline). RXR's $140M commitment signals institutional construction capital appetite for mixed-income rental (not just luxury) in South Florida, reducing cost-of-capital for developers and likely spurring competing projects. However, 40%+ AMI-priced units mean income-restricted rents cap upside; developers should focus deal flow on sub-$2M development sites in Live Local-eligible zones to maintain pro-forma integrity and maximize tax-credit equity stacking.

stories.title: Vornado Sells 49% Stake in 90 Park Avenue to Sixth Street, DivcoWest
stories.excerpt: Vornado Realty Trust has new partners at one of its Midtown office properties. The firm has sold a 49 percent stake in 90 Park Avenue, its 41-story Class A office building three blocks south of Grand Central Terminal, to Sixth Street and DivcoWest at a valuation of $722.5 million. Vornado announced the transaction Tuesday, not identifying the buyers, but sources later confirmed Sixth Street and DivcoWest are the lucky two. Eastdil Secured Savills’ Gary Phillips and Will Silverman repped Vornado — which will retain a majority stake in the property and also continue to lease and manage it — in the transaction, which is expected to close in December. Newmark’s Adam Spies, Josh King and Adam Doneger represented Sixth Street in the deal. Located a hop, skip and a jump from Grand Central, the 41-story, 990,000-square-foot 90 Park Avenue underwent a $70 million capital improvement program in 2016 that included a modernized lobby, destination elevators and upgraded mechanical systems. The building’s current occupancy rate is around 95 percent, sources said. In March 2025, alternative investment firm Balbec Capital signed a 13,200-square-foot lease to move its New York City office to 90 Park Avenue, while Swiss commodities trading and mining company Glencore also took 44,968 square feet at the property that month. In conjunction with the sale, a $500 million nonrecourse loan is in the works, according to a release from Vornado, with the firm banking on net proceeds of $575 million after costs and loan reserves. Further info on said loan couldn’t be gleaned. Eastdil, Newmark, Sixth Street and DivcoWest declined to comment. Cathy Cunningham can be reached at ccunningham@commercialobserver.com and Isabelle Durso can be reached at idurso@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Vornado sells 49% of 90 Park Avenue, Manhattan to Sixth Street and DivcoWest; $722.5M valuation.
41-story Class A office, 990,000 SF, 3 blocks south of Grand Central Terminal.
$70M capex 2016 (lobby, elevators, mechanical); Vornado retains 51% and continues management.
stories.summary: Vornado Realty Trust sold a 49 percent stake in 90 Park Avenue, its 41-story Class A office building three blocks south of Grand Central Terminal, to Sixth Street and DivcoWest at a $722.5 million valuation. The 990,000-square-foot property underwent a $70 million capital improvement program in 2016 and remains Vornado-managed. The transaction is expected to close in December 2026.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to multifamily development. This is a Midtown Manhattan office transaction. However, Sixth Street and DivcoWest's willingness to co-invest in a trophy-asset office building signals that institutional capital remains confident in Midtown's Class A office recovery and CBD fundamentals long-term, which could reduce pressure to convert prime Manhattan office to residential and preserve office stock in core submarkets. Multifamily developers should focus conversion efforts on secondary/Class B CBD office, not trophy assets where fundamentals are strengthening.
